concepts.name: Blocker to opponent's value range
concepts.example: Having an Ace blocks AA, AK, AQ combinations
concepts.application: Good for bluffing - A5s is better bluff than 76s because Ace blocks strong Ax

concepts.name: Blocker to opponent's calling range
concepts.example: Having K♠ blocks flush draws on a spade board
concepts.application: Better for value betting - opponent less likely to have flush

concepts.name: Blocker to opponent's bluffing range
concepts.example: Having a low card like 4♠ blocks some straight draws
concepts.application: Better for calling - opponent has fewer bluffs, but also fewer value hands

concepts.name: Backdoor blocker effects
concepts.example: Having A♠ on a K♠7♦2♣ board blocks backdoor nut flush draws
concepts.impact: Slightly reduces opponent's nut flush draw combos
concepts.application: Small edge in flop decisions - use for marginal bluff selection

examples.reasoning: Ace blocks AA (from 6 combos to 3), AK (from 16 to 12), AQ (16 to 12). This makes A5s a better 4-bet bluff than hands like 76s.
examples.frequency: Use A5s as 4-bet bluff ~15-20% of time vs tight 3-bet range

examples.reasoning: A♠ blocks the nut flush (A♠Xs) and AQ blocks some KQ/KJ value combos. Good bluff candidate with blocker effects.
examples.frequency: Bluff more often when holding key blockers to opponent's value range

examples.reasoning: K♠ blocks some flush combos. However, having K high also blocks some of opponent's bluff range. Net effect is small.
examples.frequency: Blockers are one factor among many - don't overweight them
